title: Choose the blog structure
question: All three keep the Activity Ledger identity and sort every article newest first. Choose the reading structure to carry into implementation.

options.label: Annotated Chronology
options.lineage: research log chronology with margin annotations
options.thesis: A continuous dated reading ledger where every article feels like a new entry in an evolving body of work.
options.viewport: A compact Writing masthead gives way immediately to a vertical date spine; the newest three articles occupy ruled rows with title, abstract, topic, reading time, and a clear open action.
options.risk: A long archive can feel repetitive unless year markers and row density create a strong cadence.

options.label: Reference Manual Index
options.lineage: tabbed technical manuals and printed subject indexes
options.thesis: The blog becomes a compact technical reference whose chronology is visible but whose topics are effortless to scan.
options.viewport: A narrow year-and-topic register sits beside a dense newest-first article index; extended tabs mark the active year while each row exposes date, category, title, and summary.
options.risk: The reference density needs careful mobile adaptation so navigation never competes with reading.

options.label: Open Reading Dossier
options.lineage: an analyst's active case file followed by its evidence register
options.thesis: The newest article receives one decisive editorial moment, while the rest remain a disciplined chronological archive.
options.viewport: The latest article opens as a broad paper dossier with title, premise, date, topic, and read action; directly below, all remaining posts continue newest first as a compact ledger.
options.risk: The featured entry must stay editorial rather than turning into a generic hero card.
